body:
TWO THINGS. I WAS WRONG ABOUT DRAFT, AND PIPELINE 318 HAS FAILED IN A WAY THAT
SETTLES THE DEADLINE QUESTION.

1. THE DRAFT ERROR IS MINE AND I VERIFIED IT RATHER THAN ACCEPTING YOUR
CORRECTION:

    origin/main aida-core/src/lifecycle.rs:227
    matches!(from, State::Approved | State::Planned | State::InProgress
                 | State::Done | State::NeedsAttention)
    grep for Draft in the body: 0

Draft is not in the set. My #2060 finding said "BUG-1568 is currently DRAFT,
which IS in the five-state set" and that was false.

THE MECHANISM OF MY ERROR IS WORSE THAN A SLIP: I READ THAT PREDICATE IN THE
SOURCE MYSELF THIS MORNING — it is the re-assertion you asked me for, and I
quoted the five states back to you verbatim. Then I generalised from the two
cases I had checked since (BUG-1480 and TASK-1289, both NeedsAttention, both
members) into "roughly everything in flight". I had the exact list and used a
remembered summary of it instead. That is the artefact-versus-recollection
failure I have been naming all day, applied to a fact I personally verified.

AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS MY 5202: a real thing, remembered in the wrong
role. I am going to stop quoting predicates from memory in findings — if it is
load-bearing enough to record, it is worth the grep.

2. PIPELINE 318 FAILED — AND THE RESULT IS FAR MORE USEFUL THAN A RED.

    test awaiting_notice_does_not_read_an_open_stdin_pipe ... FAILED
    "awaiting --notice remained alive for 3.135800526s with an open stdin pipe"

    ...and in the SAME RUN:
    PASS [13.422s] awaiting_notice_tracks_real_lease_through_session_end

THE WATCHDOG FIX WORKS FOR ITS TARGET AND BREAKS A SIBLING. The test that
failed at 1s now passes at 10s. A different test in the same file now fails
BECAUSE the process stays alive too long.

SO THE TWO TESTS PIN OPPOSITE ENDS OF THE SAME CONSTANT:

    tracks_real_lease_through_session_end   needs it LONG enough to finish a
                                            real-store read   (fails at 1s)
    does_not_read_an_open_stdin_pipe        needs it SHORT enough to exit
                                            promptly          (fails at 10s)

THERE IS NO SINGLE VALUE THAT SATISFIES BOTH. Raising the constant was not
under-argued — it is not available. That answers the question you told the
implementer to argue, and it answers it against 10s.

THE REMEDY IS THE FALLBACK I OFFERED AND YOU RECORDED: separate the test's
need from the product's bound. Inject the deadline so the slow-store test can
have a long one while the product path keeps a bound that honours BUG-1239's
fail-open contract — and the stdin test keeps a short one. A magic constant
cannot serve a 10s worst-case turn AND a promptness assertion; an injected one
can.

I have re-recorded #2019 at 442a63243c as CHANGES REQUESTED with the CI
finding pending. It is now RESOLVED-AND-FAILING rather than pending: I will
update the verdict with this result. The fix restored the dropped commit, the
commit fixes its target, and the pipeline is red for a NEW reason that the
commit caused.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: Draft error is mine (verified: not in the set) - I quoted a predicate I had personally read. AND pipeline 318 settles the deadline: 10s fixes one test and BREAKS a sibling that needs it short
